scope: Accepted 1856–1857 batch 09 source-text rendering, enclosure attribution, chronology and receipt requirements only; candidate for root review. No converter, export, transcript, corpus, training, embedding or paid-service work.

requirements.case: complete six-part enclosure and Darwin authorship
requirements.requirement: Render the copied enclosure as six complete retained sections I–VI plus its final qualification. The actual nodes are /html/body/div[7]/div/div/div/div/div[2]/div/div[3]/div[1]/div/div[2]/p[1] through p[6]; they cover human selection, a hypothetical perfect selector, natural selection, environmental change and extinction, objections, and divergence. The concluding scholarly paragraph at /html/body/div[7]/div/div/div/div/div[2]/div/div[3]/div[1]/div/div[2]/p[8] limits the abstract to selection's accumulative power and calls conclusions about primordial variation partial and imperfect. Preserve the Norman copyist / Darwin correction boundary: C.D. is Darwin-composed content copied and corrected by Ebenezer Norman, not Norman's scientific voice. Later 1858 publication is apparatus and must not be rendered as contemporary availability.

requirements.case: returned papers, First Lessons reading and expected Naturalised Plants continuation
requirements.requirement: Keep P8's custody and reading stages separate: Darwin says Watson's papers and Gray's First Lessons were safely received and that he is now reading the latter, while the final part of Gray's Naturalised Plants paper is still absent. A request or expectation of a further article is not evidence that earlier Statistics material was never received. The July 7 dispatch in 2120 is a separate event, and its passenger-to-Liverpool route must not be converted into a physical receipt date for Darwin.

requirements.case: November 29 missing Gray prompt and later Bishop witness
requirements.requirement: Keep DCP-LETT-2176 as an unpaired Darwin letter whose current Gray criticism, seed/specimen material and offer to redo the close-species list are not preserved. Do not reconstruct that incoming letter from August 2129 or proximity. The barnacle account is explicitly something Darwin heard yesterday (November 28), so a later December 3 Bishop-to-Bate report cannot be its prompt or a same-day knowledge source. implementation_boundary: Preserve enclosure section boundaries, copyist and Darwin-composed voice, plain numeric strings and later editorial/publication layers as separately addressable evidence.
Keep dispatch, receipt, reading, expected future material and missing incoming prompts distinct; no rendering requirement creates a relationship or knowledge activation.
Do not turn the December 3 Bishop witness into the missing November Gray prompt, and do not use publication history to backdate availability.
notes: The accepted September 5 Darwin output has two direct incoming scopes: 2129 supplies the natural-selection and Adlumia response, while 2120 supplies the returned Watson papers and First Lessons acknowledgement; these must remain separate sections of one output.
DCP-LETT-2129 to DCP-LETT-2125 is already accepted in batch 08 and is retained context, not a new batch 09 relationship.
